wd_people.label: Melba Liston
wd_people.description: American jazz trombonist, musical arranger, and composer (1926–1999)
wd_people.wp_abstract: Melba Doretta Liston (January 13, 1926 – April 23, 1999) was an American jazz trombonist, arranger, and composer. She was the first woman trombonist to play alongside men in big bands during the 1940s and 1960s, but as her career progressed she became better known as an arranger, particularly in partnership with pianist Randy Weston. Other major artists with whom she worked include Dizzy Gillespie, Billie Holiday, John Coltrane, and Count Basie.

community.label: Swinging Big Band Era
community.summary: This community centers on the apex of the big band era and the subsequent rise of bebop, dominated by major bandleaders and virtuoso soloists who defined mainstream jazz. Members are bound by extensive professional collaborations in touring orchestras and the vibrant New York and Chicago club scenes during the mid-20th century.
